summary: Server only. How factions stand to each other. A faction is a number from 1 to 65535 your resources give to NPCs (Npc.faction) and players (Player.faction). Two factions are hostile, friendly or neutral to each other, and a faction is always friendly to itself. An NPC with an aggroRange attacks the members of hostile factions it sees and helps the members of friendly ones in a fight. The game's own factions do not take part: KCDS NPCs fight only whom the server names.

setRelation.summary: Sets how two factions stand to each other, both ways: 'hostile' (NPCs of one with an aggroRange attack the members of the other), 'friendly' (they help each other in a fight) or 'neutral' (neither; the default). It lasts until changed or until the resource that set it stops. Throws a RangeError for a faction outside 1 to 65535 or an unknown relation, and an Error for a faction with itself.
setRelation.exampleLua:
-- server
local Faction = kcds.characters.Faction
local BANDITS = 10
local VILLAGE = 11
local WATCH = 12

Faction.setRelation(BANDITS, VILLAGE, "hostile")
Faction.setRelation(BANDITS, WATCH, "hostile")
Faction.setRelation(VILLAGE, WATCH, "friendly")

relation.summary: How faction a stands to faction b: 'hostile', 'friendly' or 'neutral'. A faction is friendly to itself, and 0 (no faction) is neutral to every faction. Throws a RangeError for a faction outside 0 to 65535.
relation.exampleLua:
-- server
if kcds.characters.Faction.relation(npc.faction, player.faction) == "hostile" then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToPlayer(player, npc.name .. " draws a weapon.")
end

relations.summary: The pairs of factions that are not neutral, as { a, b, relation } with a below b.
relations.exampleLua:
-- server
for _, pair in ipairs(kcds.characters.Faction.relations()) do
  print(pair.a .. " and " .. pair.b .. ": " .. pair.relation)
end
